english: when you, bought up from everywhere, the noble
problem: nobilis is most naturally acc. pl. (= nobiles) with libros, 'the noble books of Panaetius'; the note's genitive with Panaeti is the weaker construal. The English line is neutral; the note is the issue.
suggested: when you, bought up from everywhere, the noble (note: nobilis = nobiles, acc. pl. with libros, line 14)

problem: segetes is accusative (object of poscit/orat), so opimae cannot be nom. pl. with it; opimae is genitive with Sardiniae ('of rich Sardinia'), and feracis = feraces, acc. pl. with segetes ('fertile crops'). The adjectives are swapped.
Same case error: feracis agrees with segetes (acc. pl.), not with Sardiniae.

english: son of Leto, may you grant, and, I pray, with sound
problem: 'with' renders cum, which stands on line 19 (integra cum mente); a word moved across the line break.
suggested: son of Leto, may you grant, and, I pray, sound

english: mind, neither a shameful old age
problem: cum ('with') omitted here because it was moved up to line 18.
suggested: with mind, neither a shameful old age
